I've been working this land for 40 years. I know Quzhou's soil and weather like I know my own hands. Let me think through what I'll do this season.

My 5 mu splits naturally: 2 mu for cotton — that's my cash crop and why I call myself a cotton farmer — and 3 mu in the wheat-maize rotation. The kids in the city can't always come back for busy periods, so I need to be realistic about my labor. At 65 my back isn't what it was.

**Cotton (2 mu):** I'll plant Bt hybrid cotton again. It cuts down the bollworm spraying, which matters when I'm working mostly alone. I apply base fertilizer before planting — phosphorus and potassium worked into the bed — then split my nitrogen across topdressing at squaring and boll-setting. Four irrigations: at planting, flowering, early boll, late boll. I'll still spray four or five times — aphids don't care about Bt — but it's manageable. I'll rotary till rather than deep plough. My target is 250 jin of seed cotton per mu. That's what this land gives me if I do it right.

**Winter wheat (3 mu):** I plant in October after I've deep-ploughed with a hired tractor. Improved variety from the county seed station — I stopped saving my own seed years ago, the yields just weren't there. Four irrigations: winter water before the freeze, then jointing, heading, and grain fill. Two pesticide passes for powdery mildew and aphids. I expect 450 kg/mu.

**Summer maize (3 mu, same land as wheat):** Soon as wheat comes off in June I get the maize in without ploughing — no time to lose moisture and I don't have the labor for a full tillage pass. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan or whatever the ag-supply has this year. Three irrigations if the summer rains are weak. Two sprays for armyworm. I expect 550 kg/mu.
